I'm designing a motion/"juice" system (animations, shader accents, interaction variants) for Twyne, a Qwik + TipTap/ProseMirror local-first writing app at /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne. Brand: editorial, letterpress, literary writer's room (paper, ink, stamps, vermilion/cobalt). I need a precise inventory of the **manuscript text surface** — what happens as the writer types, moves the mouse, selects, scrolls, and drags — so I can add identity-carrying motion without harming writing. Do not edit anything.

Scope:
- `src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx` (4700 lines — grep, don't read whole): extension list, caret/gapcursor, onUpdate scheduling (scheduleLiveMeta / scheduleDerive), drag and drop handling (files, blocks, images), paste, pointer handlers, comment/citation/suggestion marks and how they are clicked, the selection popover, zen mode CSS (around line 450), the `.twyne-mark-anchor` chips.
- `src/components/editor/extensions/*` (list each extension and what it decorates), `manuscript-panel.tsx`, `selection-actions.tsx`, `slash-command-menu.tsx`, `suggestion-panel.tsx`, `user-comment-panel.tsx`, `persona-note-panel.tsx`, `find-replace-panel.tsx`, `grammar-panel.tsx`, `document-outline.tsx`, `image-inspector.tsx`, `floating-table-toolbar.tsx`, `insert-panels.tsx`, `forecast-line.tsx`.
- `src/components/in-flow/*` (flow-surface, flow-ribbon, margin-rail, passage-gather, sentence-bench, thread-instrument, tool-renderer): what "flow" states exist (`data-flow`), how typing-vs-idle is detected, what appears in the margins.
- Relevant global.css rules (src/global.css is 10k lines — grep: `.ProseMirror`, `.page-canvas`, `.manuscript-scroller`, `.twyne-comment-mark`, `.citation-mark`, `.drag-overlay`, `twyne-gapcursor`, `selection`, `::selection`, `caret-color`, `.zen-mode`).

For EACH component/sub-element report compactly:
1. file:line, what it shows.
2. Triggers: typing, caret move, selection, hover, click, scroll, drag, keyboard.
3. Current feedback/motion (class names, keyframes, global.css line numbers), and busy/error/success variants.
4. Consequence class of actions: local-only edit, sends text to an AI provider / spends hosted credits, syncs/collab, destructive.
5. Performance-sensitive paths (anything that runs per keystroke; whether decorations re-render; IME/composition handling).

Also answer specifically: Is there a custom caret? Does anything track scroll position (scroll listeners, IntersectionObserver)? Is there paragraph drag-handle reordering? What is the CSS for `::selection` and caret-color? What fonts/colours does the page use?

Return a structured, terse list with file:line references. Under ~1500 words.

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.

Here is the inventory, cited as file:line. `TE` = `src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx`, `G` = `src/global.css`, `ext/` = `src/components/editor/extensions/`. ## Short answers - **Custom caret:** No. The browser caret is used everywhere. `caret-color: var(--color-vermilion)` is set only on the illuminated drop-cap span (G:861). The numeric stepper input uses cobalt (G:5715). The ProseMirror body has no `caret-color`, so the caret takes the ink colour. - **Caret-like things that do exist:** - Dropcursor: StarterKit config at TE:1245, 2px wide, class `twyne-dropcursor`, vermilion with a 25% halo (G:716). - Gapcursor: a 1.25rem vermilion bar with `twyne-gapcursor-blink` 1.1s `steps(2)`, turned off under reduced motion (G:723-755). - A `▍` caret on flow cards (`flow-caret`, G:8370-8379). `persona-reply-caret` (G:9721) is used for streaming replies. - **`::selection`:** There is no global rule, so selection uses the system colour. The only rule is `.twyne-illuminated-initial::selection { background: var(--color-vermilion-light, #c1272d30) }` (G:885). The Typst CodeMirror editor styles its own selection (`typst-code-editor.ts:497`). - **Scroll tracking:** There is no IntersectionObserver in the editor (the only one is on the landing page). Four scroll listeners: - TE:3174, passive on `.manuscript-scroller`. Batched to one rAF; repositions comment and suggestion popovers. Also a ResizeObserver on the canvas. - `flow-surface.tsx:775`, passive. Runs `layout()` for margin cards and connectors, plus a linger timer and a ResizeObserver (:729). - `floating-table-toolbar.tsx:360`, capture on window. - `passage-gather.tsx:348`, capture on document, only while the sheet is open. - `margin-rail.tsx:159` uses a ResizeObserver only. - **Paragraph drag reordering:** No paragraph handles. There are **section (heading) drag handles** in `ext/section-reorder.ts:40-53`: - A `⋮⋮` widget at every heading, with inline style (opacity .55, `cursor:grab`) and no CSS class rules. - The drop indicator is an inline 2px line in `var(--accent-color,#6d5dfc)` (:84). That purple fallback is off-brand. - It uses the custom MIME `application/x-twyne-section`. - Ordinary text drag-and-drop uses ProseMirror's native behaviour. - **Fonts (G:62-66):** - Display: Libre Baskerville - Body serif: Lora (the manuscript, 1.125rem, line-height 1.8, `onum`/`liga`/`kern`, justified, hyphenated; G:804-822) - UI: DM Sans - Mono: JetBrains Mono - Labels: Special Elite (typewriter) - **Colours (G:18-35):** paper `#f4ecd8` (paper-2 `#ebe1c9`, paper-3 `#ddd0b1`, paper-soft `#faf3df`), ink `#1f1b16` (ink-light `#4a3f33`, ink-muted `#8a7e6c`), vermilion `#c1272d`, cobalt `#2c4a7c`. Alternate themes are at G:217, 241 and 267 (the last is dark: paper `#191714`, vermilion `#e2686c`). Paper grain is mixed from ink at G:189. ## Update path (runs per keystroke) - `onUpdate` (TE:1368) calls: - `scheduleLiveMeta`: leading-edge throttle, 200ms, `getText()` for the word count (TE:980). - `scheduleDerive`: 500ms debounce with a 2500ms max wait (TE:1017). One `getHTML()` feeds the comment reconcile, the mirror/persistence, citation detection, and the `twyne:content` event. It flushes on `pagehide`/`visibilitychange` (TE:1052). - `transaction` → `refreshActive` (TE:1643): about 20 `isActive` checks plus `can().undo/redo` on **every transaction**, including caret moves. It also calls `refreshSelectionAction` unless a pointer is down. - `transaction` → `refreshSlashMenu` (TE:1704): one `coordsAtPos` per transaction. - `update` → structure refresh, 300ms debounce: outline, notes and Mermaid (TE:1672). - `update` → popover reposition via rAF (TE:3176), and row-resize handle refresh (TE:2293, synchronous per update). - flow-conductor `onTransaction` (`ext/flow-conductor.ts:509`) logs insert/delete samples on docChanged. It skips y-sync and non-history transactions. There is also a 1s tick (:127) and window listeners for `pointermove`/`keydown` (:1669-1670). - **Decorations rebuilt on every docChanged:** - `mark-anchor-widgets` (full rebuild). - `section-reorder` (calls `buildDocumentOutline` per doc change). - `quick-review` (clears to empty). - remote-cursors and find-replace map or rebuild on docChanged. - living-desk only maps positions; it recomputes after a 400ms delay plus `requestIdleCallback`. - **IME/composition:** `editor.view.composing` is checked in quick-review (`ext/quick-review.ts:231`, retries in 300ms) and struggle-tracker (`ext/struggle-tracker.ts:271`). Nothing else checks it: no `compositionstart` listener, and the derive/live-meta schedulers keep running during composition. ## Manuscript surface (TE) - **Zen mode:** TE:448-480. It is **on by default** (`zenMode: true`, TE:428). It removes backgrounds and underlines from persona notes, comment marks, citations, suggestions and endnotes, and sets the toolbar to `opacity .15`. Further zen rules: G:3048 (mark anchors), 6881 (ruler), 7361 (quick-review marker), 7813 (in-flow rails), 10056-10071 (page-canvas border). It is toggled by the `view.zen` shortcut (TE:3906), and the flow conductor also sets it (`flow-conductor.ts:470`). - **Hover on marks:** a delegated `mouseover`/`mouseout` on the editor element (TE:2010-2090) opens the persona-note and writer-comment popovers. - Hover is disarmed while typing: printable keys, Backspace and Enter set `hoverArmed=false` (TE:2172). - It re-arms after more than 3px of mouse movement (TE:2205). - Zen mode suppresses it. - **Click:** TE:2094. A click on a `.twyne-mark-anchor` chip opens the comment, note or suggestion card by `data-anchor-kind`. A click on the mark text falls through to caret placement.
